The D.A. of Bamberg investigates two Syrian asylum seekers for financing terrorism. The two men, 22 and 23 years old, last Monday invaded the home of the owner of a floor tiler business, placed on the business property in Redwitz, and stole several thousand Euro. According to the D.A. that part of the loot should be used "to finance warfare against Assad's troups in Syria". Additionally, the two migrants are under investigation for aggravated robbery.

It is still unclear if they planned to finance IS. "We aren't far enough in our investigations yet," tells Bamberg D.A. Christopher Rosenbusch.

The two men are accused of having invaded the home using mace and to have taken money from the safe. Both men could have been arrested on the following morning. A 52 years old German woman, who had given one of the Syrians a ride, is currently under investigation for accessory to the robbery. On request of the local D.A. a judge issued an arrest warrant against the two men.

Both suspects are in pre-trial custody. After finding leads towards plans to finance warfare in Syria by the 23 year old man (an employee at the floor tiler business), the D.A. of Bamberg took the case over, being in charge of terrorism felonies.

The entered the business property masked with baclavas. Inside the building, they overwhelmed the 67 year old business owner, tied him up and blindfolded him. They then used brutal force to open the safe. In addition to money, they stole jewelry. They managed to flee, but the owner could free himself and alarm the police. Near Hochstadt their car could be stopped.

Cash and a baclava have been confiscated. In the flats of the two asylum seekers in Lichtenfels and Redwitz additional evidence was found, among it the remainder of the loot hidden in a hollow space withiin the wall. The asylum seekers have already partially confessed.
